payload.title: Auto-resolve expectedVersion on writeObject to standardize optimistic concurrency
payload.description:
Today FrickClient.writeObject sends POST without an if-match header when the caller doesn't pass `expectedVersion`. Against types whose schema declares `mergePolicy: "versionPrecondition"` (the default for RangerCRM's entire schema), every UPDATE returns 409 storage.conflict. Apps that try to behave as last-write-wins — like RangerCRM's FrickAccountStore.upsert, which is explicitly documented as "Last-write-wins (no optimistic-concurrency token)" — silently fail on every edit.

Framework already has the version. `FrickSQLiteStorage.local_objects` carries `version INTEGER NOT NULL` per (type, id), and writeObject already calls `storage.saveObjectData(... version: envelope.version)` after every successful write. The framework just doesn't read it back.

## Proposal

1. Add `func loadObjectVersion(type: String, id: String) throws -> Int?` to the `FrickStorage` protocol, with a `FrickSQLiteStorage` impl that does a single indexed lookup against `local_objects`.

2. In `FrickClient.writeObject`, when the caller passes no `expectedVersion`, transparently resolve one from storage before building the request:
   ```swift
   let effectiveExpectedVersion: Int? = expectedVersion
       ?? (try? storage.loadObjectVersion(type: type, id: id))
   ```

3. No new policy parameter; no breaking API change. Callers that already pass `expectedVersion` (planning their own optimistic-concurrency) are unaffected. Callers that pass nil (the vast majority — RangerCRM and every store like it) get correct expectedVersion automatically on update, eliminating the spurious 409s.

## Behavior matrix after the change

| Caller        | Object cached locally | Object exists on server | Today                        | After                          |
|---------------|-----------------------|-------------------------|------------------------------|--------------------------------|
| passes nil    | no                    | no                      | POST, 201 create             | unchanged                      |
| passes nil    | no                    | yes                     | POST, **409 conflict**       | POST + if-match: (refetch)…    |
| passes nil    | yes (we wrote it)     | yes (same version)      | POST, **409 conflict**       | POST + if-match: v, 200 update |
| passes nil    | yes (stale)           | yes (newer)             | POST, **409 conflict**       | POST + if-match: stale, 409    |
| passes value  | (anything)            | (anything)              | POST + if-match: v           | unchanged                      |

The "cached-stale" row stays a 409 — that's a true conflict another writer caused, and surfacing it lets the app decide whether to refetch-and-retry or merge. Frame "we never read this object" (row 2) the same way for now — it's rare, and the app can add a refetch loop on top if it wants the truly-zero-config experience.

## Why no `onConflict` policy parameter

Considered adding `.fail` / `.clobber` with `.clobber` doing a refetch-and-retry. Rejected for v1: it conflates "I want last-write-wins" with "I want auto-retry," and the right policy varies per app. With auto-resolve in place, apps that want clobber semantics can wrap upsert in a single trivial retry helper (or open a follow-up if a pattern emerges).

## Downstream impact

RangerCRM (`/Users/bri/dev/RangerCRM`): no app changes. Every Frick*Store.upsert immediately starts succeeding on edits. Unblocks RCRM-132/135 verification at the rename step (POST /objects/Account/<id> currently 409s).
